about: Satisfied Seal is a tight close-up of a grey, speckled seal with its eyes squeezed shut, whiskers fanned out and the corners of its mouth turned up in a smug little smile. It looks completely at peace with the world, like it just sank into a warm bath. People caption it with small, specific wins that feel disproportionately good: a build that passes on the first try, finding cash in an old jacket, the exact parking spot you wanted. The joke is the size of the bliss compared to the size of the victory.
usage:
Split one sentence across the two boxes. The top box sets the scene ("when the build", "when the pizza"), and the bottom box delivers the tiny triumph ("passes first try", "arrives early"). The seal's face supplies the emotion, so you don't need to say "I feel great".

It works best with low-stakes, very relatable pleasures: peeling the protective film off a new screen, a meeting ending ten minutes early, a cable that plugs in the right way the first time. Big achievements make the image feel smaller; tiny ones make it perfect.
